items.title: For a derived complete object the vanishing above degree zero can be checked after tensoring with the Koszul complex
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a finitely generated ideal I = (f_1, ..., f_r) of a ring A and a derived complete object K of D(A), and establishes the equivalence of three conditions: that H^i(K) vanish for i > 0; that H^i(K tensor^L_A A/I) vanish for i > 0; and that H^i(K tensor^L_A K_1^bullet) vanish for i > 0, where K_1^bullet is the Koszul object of the ambient situation (source lines 26436-26446). The implication (1) implies (2) is immediate, and (2) implies (3) is exactly the bounded-above-mod-I lemma (proof lines 26449-26450). The substantive direction is (3) implies (1). For s = 0, ..., r the proof considers the objects K(s) = K tensor^L_A K_bullet(A, f_1, ..., f_s) where K_bullet(A, f_1, ..., f_s) is the Koszul complex placed in cohomological degrees -s, ..., 0, and obtains distinguished triangles K(s-1) --f_s--> K(s-1) -> K(s) -> K(s-1)[1] from the cone-of-Koszul lemma (proof lines 26451-26461). Two inductions then run in opposite directions: an ascending induction on s from K(0) = K being derived complete shows every K(s) is derived complete (proof lines 26461-26463), and a descending induction shows that K(s) has no nonzero cohomology in degrees greater than 0, the case s = r being exactly assumption (3); if it holds for K(s) with s > 0, then the multiplication map f_s on H^i(K(s-1)) is surjective for i > 0, and the serre-subcategory and derived-complete-zero lemmas then force H^i(K(s-1)) to vanish (proof lines 26463-26468). The non-routine content is the interplay of the two inductions along the Koszul triangles, with the surjectivity of multiplication producing vanishing because the object is derived complete.
